question: Which of these posts cover hybrid inverters?
answer:
The page leads with "How to Choose Between a Hybrid Inverter and an AC-Coupled Storage Setup", its latest post, which compares hybrid-inverter and AC-coupled storage architectures for residential and small-commercial projects, so installers can pick the right topology.

Beyond that, the closest related reading is "What Installers Should Check Before Pairing an Inverter with Battery Storage", a pre-installation checklist on inverter-to-battery compatibility, communication protocols, cable sizing and site preparation. Topically adjacent but not about hybrid inverters as such are the storage sizing, indoor-versus-outdoor battery, commissioning and monitoring pieces.

The page groups everything under system design, battery storage, installation and commissioning, and monitoring and energy management, and offers a search over all posts, plus a route into the Solution Configurator if the reading turns into a project.

question: Welche dieser Beiträge behandeln Hybrid-Wechselrichter?
answer:

Der Beitrag ist als praktischer Vergleich der beiden Architekturen angelegt und soll Installateuren bei der Wahl der passenden Topologie für Wohn- und kleine Gewerbeprojekte helfen; er ist unter den neuesten Beiträgen gelistet und mit dem Schlagwort Hybrid-Wechselrichter versehen.

question: Summarize this post
answer:
This post is a practical comparison of the two storage architectures, written for installers working on residential and small-commercial projects. It defines a hybrid inverter as a single unit that combines the solar inverter and the battery inverter, handling DC input from the panels, feeding AC loads and routing surplus into the battery. An AC-coupled setup, by contrast, keeps a dedicated solar inverter for the panels and uses a separate battery inverter, with the two communicating over the AC bus — the usual retrofit path when storage is added to an existing PV installation.

On selection, the post recommends hybrid for new installations: fewer components, simpler wiring and higher round-trip efficiency, since energy is converted only once between DC and AC. It notes that switchover time to backup differs by model and points to the datasheet on each product page for that value. AC-coupled is recommended when a working solar inverter is already in place and batteries are to be added without replacing existing hardware, at the cost of slightly lower efficiency and more involved commissioning.

The closing checklist for installers covers battery compatibility, maximum charge and discharge rates, grid-code settings, and whether the chosen topology supports backup during a grid outage. The post was published on 29 May 2026.

question: Summarize this page
answer:
This page presents Linker as the storage solution partner behind installers' projects in Germany. It covers residential hybrid storage in single- and three-phase versions as well as commercial battery cabinets of up to 261 kWh per unit, and it lists system packages with inverter, battery and metering platforms together with the compatibility lists on file.

Two tools are described for preparing an installation before ordering: the Roof detail step, which maps the layout from site conditions, and the Solution Configurator, which sizes inverter and battery capacity to actual energy loads and produces the bill of materials; Genie is named alongside them for wiring references from the manuals on file. The page then walks through the project stages — layout around site requirements, electrical sizing in the configurator, transparent project pricing, equipment dispatched to your installation schedule, and support continuing through commissioning.

The partnership is described in several parts: checking component combinations against the compatibility lists, technical documentation for inspection day, a supply partner that scales with your projects, technical clarification from the engineering team in Germany, warranty coordination backed by your order records, and a digital project and ordering hub. The page closes with questions installers ask before ordering and an invitation to design and source your next installation. | action:open_configurator
